correctness.rationale: Nonzero partial derivatives prove all seven diagonal forms smooth. Hessian factorization forces monomial equivalences, reducing all nonzero coefficient tuples to seven distinct scalar-permutation cube-class orbits. A unique-echelon enumeration of all 140050 rational projective lines produces the seven incidence histograms. Every individual point degree is reproduced by an independent normalized-point polar-condition enumeration of all 2801 ambient rational points. Exact double-counting checks \(\sum_j m_j=\#X(\mathbf F_7)\) and \(\sum_j j m_j=8\#F_1(X)(\mathbf F_7)\) hold for each case. Included standard-library script executed successfully. All operations are modulo 7; no infinite claim is derived from finite sampling.

originality.rationale: The claim is the complete *local rational point-line incidence profile* for all seven diagonal projective types, not solely total line counts. Existing Fano-surface zeta formulas and the established Fermat case do not determine individual point degrees; the primary finite-field study gives experimental global distributions instead. Targeted research-record and literature searches found no covering local incidence table. Classical twisted-Fermat tools and unindexed finite-geometry references remain residual risks.
residual_risks: Weil–Jacobi sum methods and existing diagonal-hypersurface geometry might yield the same local multiplicity profiles by a previously unnoticed specialization; no exhaustive negative literature claim is possible.
The classification concerns projective equivalence over F7 and may merge under abstract isomorphism; no such abstract classification is claimed.
The result does not settle whether all smooth (non-diagonal) cubic threefolds over F7 have a rational line.

value.rationale: The field F7 is explicitly left as a difficult existence case for rational lines on smooth cubic threefolds in the motivating primary literature. All seven diagonal projective types form a natural complete subfamily rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. The new local incidence invariant distinguishes a sharp line-filling dichotomy (3 fully covered types versus four with 189,135,135,162 uncovered rational points) that total Fano counts cannot determine, including two inequivalent 27-line classes with distinct profiles. The exact classification can inform geometric constructions and further finite-field incidence studies.
